thread:
morgan: Customer (ACME) opened a ticket — SSE stream yields a few events then stalls. client reconnects, sometimes receives the rest, sometimes gets duplicate chunks. Happening ~90s after start.

support_amy: Do we have the request id / client SDK? any proxy in front?

morgan: customer sent curl repro: `curl -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -N -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?session=abc123`

ingrid_sre: Paste of what they see (trimmed):
```
> GET /v1/stream?session=abc123 HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
data: {"delta":"Hello"}\n\n
data: {"delta":" world"}\n\n
// then no data for ~90s, connection still established but no more events
```

javi_eng: On our side logs show the generator is still producing tokens and pushing to the connection. Upstream ALBs show no FIN until client resets. Any chance an intermediate proxy is buffering?

ingrid_sre: I checked edge logs — we see `proxy_idle_timeout=60s` on some customer-facing ALBs, but these streams started from an internal routing tier with `keepalive=90s`. Could be mismatch.

support_amy: Customer reports they see a 200 on reconnect and include `Last-Event-ID: 42` but server resumes at 40 sometimes (duplicate) and other times at 42 (missing).

morgan: Sounds like partial flush + connection tear then replay semantics not deterministic. We should confirm whether the runtime flushes comment pings or only sends data frames.

javi_eng: Repro notes I ran locally: `socat -v - TCP:api.redwood.internal:443` then wrote a raw HTTP SSE request; observed that when we don't emit any bytes for ~30s some proxies start TCP keepalive, others just stop forwarding data. TCP keepalive is too coarse here (minutes-level on many kernels), so not reliable for quick detection.

ingrid_sre: Quick mitigation: have the stream emitter send a lightweight SSE comment ping (a colon line) every 15s. That will force many intermediaries to forward bytes and helps proxies keep the connection open. Example ping line: `: keepalive\n\n` (must be double-newline to terminate event).

support_amy: Does adding comment pings affect client behavior? Some SDKs treat any non-data as noise but should not break. Add opt-in flag?

javi_eng: Most clients ignore comments per SSE spec. We'll add a config flag `sse_keepalive_interval` default 15s for hosted API; also emit `X-Stream-Ping: comment` header in responses so older clients can opt-out.

morgan: Also we should handle last-event-id more deterministically: ensure we ack at write-time (persist sequence number once data flushed to socket). If socket write fails or buffer is still in kernel with partial data, we may have divergence.

ingrid_sre: Filed INC-1234 with steps, repro curl + tcpdump + edge logs. Proposed rollout: patch runtime to emit comment pings, adjust docs to recommend ALB idle timeout > 120s or use our pinging, and add a small client SDK helper that auto-reconnects with exponential backoff and de-duplicates based on event id.

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: sse-ping-experiment → staging (build #4521) :white_check_mark:

support_amy: Customer notified about temporary workaround (increase client-side reconnect backoff and add last-event-id handling). They'll test pinging build in staging tomorrow.

morgan: Thanks — keep me posted. If staging looks good we'll schedule a canary to prod and update the KB with reproducible curl + tcpdump snippet. :thumbsup:
